title: Modern Data Engineering for AI Systems
description: Build one cumulative Mini-Lakehouse across five evenings. Run your labs in Google Colab, compare your results, and save your progress to GitHub every day.

schedule.prayer_note: The instructor confirms the placement of both prayer breaks for the actual course dates. Keep a full 60-minute lab.

learning_outcomes.text: Compare warehouses, data lakes and Lakehouse architectures for a stated use case.
Explain compute–storage separation and its effects on cost, elasticity and scale.
learning_outcomes.evidence: A cost comparison with explicit assumptions.

learning_outcomes.text: Design an ELT pipeline for a modern cloud data environment.
learning_outcomes.evidence: Bronze-to-Silver transformations, dbt models and actual test results.

learning_outcomes.text: Implement Delta Lake tables with ACID transactions and schema enforcement.
learning_outcomes.evidence: Accepted and rejected writes, revision-aware MERGE and version evidence.

learning_outcomes.text: Develop streaming and event-driven ingestion patterns.
learning_outcomes.evidence: Kafka delivery, a Spark checkpoint restart and distinct-event evidence.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply data-quality, observability and governance controls across a pipeline.
learning_outcomes.evidence: Quality rejection, quarantine, revalidation, monitoring and governance decisions.

learning_outcomes.text: Connect Lakehouse products to AI, reporting and analytics consumers.
learning_outcomes.evidence: A reconciled BI query and time-aware AI feature inputs.

learning_outcomes.text: Build a working Mini-Lakehouse with Delta Lake and PySpark.
learning_outcomes.evidence: One cumulative project with restorable state and reproducible outputs.

activity.prompt: Place each example in Bronze, Silver or Gold: original trip file; one validated row per trip; city revenue report.
activity.answer: Original trip file: Bronze. Validated trip table: Silver. City revenue report: Gold.

days.question: Bronze contains 144 trip receipts but only 72 distinct trip IDs. How many business trips have you observed, and why keep the receipts?
days.answer: You observed 72 distinct trips delivered twice. Preserve the 144 receipt records and their source metadata so you can explain arrivals. Silver will select the business record for each trip.

days.title: ELT and trusted Silver
days.subtitle: Turn repeated receipts into reliable business records.
concepts: dbt models, tests, freshness and lineage

expected.label: Silver trips
expected.explanation: 72 base trips plus three late trips; replay adds no business trips.

expected.label: Total fares
expected.explanation: SAR 1,794.60 plus SAR 81.00 of late-trip fares.

expected.label: Final Bronze receipts
expected.explanation: Receipts record the original deliveries and the late-batch redelivery.

activity.prompt: Choose the trip business key: driver_id, trip date or trip_id. Explain one collision the wrong key would create.
activity.answer: Use trip_id. A driver can complete many trips and a date can contain many trips, so neither uniquely identifies a trip.

days.question: Silver has 75 trips after three late trips arrive. Will replaying that same late data increase the result to 78?
days.answer: No. Silver stays at 75 because the replay carries the same trip IDs and identical business values. Receipt counts may increase for a new delivery; the business count must not.

labs.title: Apply corrections and inspect Delta history

expected.label: Corrected trip fare
expected.explanation: SYN_T0001 changes from SAR 18.00 at source revision 2.

expected.label: Silver trips
expected.explanation: A correction changes one trip instead of adding another.

expected.label: Correction replay
expected.explanation: The same accepted correction does not add another SAR 5.00.

activity.prompt: Choose a response for each message: a newer approved revision; an older revision; the same revision with conflicting business values.
activity.answer: Apply the newer revision, leave the accepted value unchanged for the older revision, and reject the same-revision conflict for investigation.

days.question: A trip fare changes from SAR 18 to SAR 23. If the correction is delivered again, should the fare become SAR 28?
days.answer: No. The approved value stays SAR 23. Revision-aware MERGE applies the accepted business state; it does not repeatedly add a correction difference.

labs.title: Ingest events and resume the query

expected.label: Received message records
expected.explanation: The experiment includes two replayed messages and one new late event.

expected.label: Distinct events
expected.explanation: The two identical replayed event IDs do not become new business events.

expected.label: Quality candidate
expected.explanation: The candidate combines 75 trusted rows with seven deliberately defective rows.

expected.label: Quarantine / revalidated
expected.explanation: Record rejection reasons, then test a new clean candidate before approval.

activity.prompt: Two Kafka messages have different offsets but the same event_id and identical payloads. How many deliveries and business events do they represent?
activity.answer: They represent two deliveries and one distinct business event. Transport offsets identify records in a partition; event_id identifies the business event.

days.question: A candidate contains 82 rows and fails because seven are invalid. How can you safely use the other 75?
days.answer: Block the failed candidate, quarantine the seven rows with reasons, create a clean 75-row candidate, and run the quality gate again before approving it.

expected.label: Validated products / CSV exports
expected.explanation: Read each product contract and release manifest.

expected.label: Reconciled trips / fares
expected.explanation: Aggregated products reconcile to the same trusted trips.

expected.label: Recorded GPS events
expected.explanation: Count events by trip before joining them to fare measures.

expected.label: AI feature / label rows
expected.explanation: Feature rows use historical data. Future labels remain NULL with UNOBSERVED status.

activity.prompt: At a decision cutoff, which input is valid: completed trips already available in the past 24 hours, or the actual trip count in the next hour?
activity.answer: Use the completed trips whose source data was available by the cutoff. The actual future-hour count is a future label, not an input available at prediction time.

days.question: bi.fact_trips has 75 rows, but ai.zone_hourly_features has three. Does that mean 72 trips were lost?
days.answer: No. The products have different grain and time windows. The fact table has one row per trip; features have one row per city, cutoff and prediction horizon, using only eligible historical data.

checks_en: Read the source manifest and verify file hashes before processing.
Create real Delta Bronze tables with source and ingestion metadata.
Replay trips without overwriting history and explain the intended Bronze growth.
Record at least three quality risks; distinguish observed defects from risks.
State every assumption and separate hypothetical teaching units from currency.
Compare always-on and scheduled operation, including overhead and a counterexample.
Measure actual Spark scans with equal-result checks and query plans.
Report observed timings without promising a speed-up on a tiny dataset.
Type columns and normalize timestamps consistently; preserve raw source files.
Normalize labels and validate driver relationships before publishing Silver.
Deduplicate on a documented business key and deterministic precedence rule.
Ingest the fixed late-trip batch and demonstrate that rerunning does not duplicate results.
Observe real Delta transaction-log commits and enforce the table schema.
Reject invalid writes without silently dropping failed checks.
Apply the correction twice and compare logical table contents.
Read earlier versions and run maintenance/delete exercises only on isolated training copies.
Demonstrate an actual Kafka producer/consumer and Spark streaming source.
Assign a separate persistent checkpoint to each streaming query.
Record the observed effect of stop/restart and duplicate event deliveries.
Explain event time, processing time and late-event handling from saved evidence.
Run an actual Great Expectations suite on the intended table.
Quarantine invalid records with reasons and stop unsafe promotion.
Record quality, freshness and run-health observations against fixed scenario times.
Document lineage, ownership, intended access and retention; use synthetic data only.
Run the dependency-ordered Bronze → Silver → Gold flow.
Prove that failures prevent unsafe downstream publication.
Rerun the same logical input and reconcile content, not volatile run timestamps.
Record one recovery attempt and preserve daily evidence rather than rebuilding undocumented work.

checks_en: Prepare feature and reporting outputs with explicit grains and definitions.
